source_status: User-provided topic sequence and dates; not independently verified

formulas.name: Einstein photoelectric equation
formulas.when_to_use: To determine the maximum kinetic energy of electrons released by incident light.
common_mistakes: Using light intensity instead of frequency to set electron energy

concepts.definition: In the single-photon regime, no photoemission occurs below the material threshold hν < W_A. Multiphoton processes are outside this approximation.
Above threshold, increasing light intensity generally increases electron count; increasing frequency raises maximum electron energy.
concepts.when_to_use: The ordinary one-photon photoelectric model assumes a clean material surface.

concepts.definition: A retarding electric field can stop the most energetic emitted photoelectrons, allowing an estimate of Kmax.
concepts.when_to_use: Use the magnitude of stopping voltage; sign conventions differ.

concepts.definition: The longest vacuum wavelength capable of producing one-photon emission follows from the work function.
concepts.when_to_use: Below threshold frequency (above threshold wavelength), one-photon emission is absent.
